title: Dashboard Domain Library Registry
purpose: Define approved domain-native libraries that may be wrapped by @hermes/dashboard-kit so downstream dashboards do not rebuild complex domain behavior with static HTML, hand-drawn charts, or local one-off components.

defaultPolicy.projectLocalInstallAllowed: only when the library is wrapped through @hermes/dashboard-kit or an approved temporary exception exists
newLibraryAdmission: record the domain and candidate in this registry
explain why generic dashboard primitives are insufficient
declare visual proof and interaction proof expectations
declare license and bundle/performance review status
add or update validator coverage before promotion

domains.label: Financial And Trading Charts

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Financial-native chart behavior is a core requirement for market, OANDA, and trading screens. Generic SVG line charts are not acceptable for this domain.
tradeoffs: does not provide market data
does not provide built-in indicators
dashboard kit must own indicator calculations and data adapters

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Use only when the product requires a full TradingView-like terminal and the licensing/integration constraints are accepted.
tradeoffs: heavier integration
commercial/licensing review required
less owned design control

bannedFallbacks: div-based sparkline as primary trading chart

domains.label: General Dashboard Charts

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Good default for business dashboards where charts need to be reliable, readable, and fast to compose inside shared components.
tradeoffs: less suitable for highly custom visual systems
large dense datasets may need specialized handling

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Use when Recharts cannot meet the visual or interaction requirement and dashboard kit needs deeper control over chart primitives.
tradeoffs: more engineering effort
requires us to build more complete chart components

bannedFallbacks: chart without axes when axes are meaningful
single chart type reused for every comparison

domains.label: Data Tables And Evidence Grids

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Headless table behavior lets the dashboard kit enforce our own visual standard while getting reliable table state management.
tradeoffs: not a finished visual table
dashboard kit must own markup, spacing, density, and toolbar patterns

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Use when a table becomes a true grid workspace with heavy volume, complex columns, or operational editing.
tradeoffs: can overpower the product design
some advanced features require enterprise licensing

bannedFallbacks: plain table over ten rows without pagination
header sort controls repeated noisily when toolbar sort is required

domains.label: Calendar And Scheduling

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Calendar behavior is a domain problem. FullCalendar prevents us from rebuilding month/week/day mechanics by hand.
tradeoffs: premium plugins may require license
must be heavily themed through dashboard-kit tokens

libraryCandidates.whyUse: A lighter alternative for projects that need basic event scheduling without heavier FullCalendar features.
tradeoffs: less complete for advanced planning workflows
more custom behavior may be needed

bannedFallbacks: day cells with noisy status text instead of concise state
planning form without drawer or focused detail region

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Drag/drop should be controlled by product state and styled by dashboard-kit, not by a finished third-party board skin.
tradeoffs: provides behavior rather than finished UI
accessibility and keyboard paths must be validated

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Use when workflows need more complex drag item types or drop target semantics than simple sortable lists.
tradeoffs: more boilerplate
heavier mental model

domains.label: Node Graphs And Pipelines

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Story construction and agent workflows need editable node/edge behavior. Static diagrams cannot support operational research work.
tradeoffs: must be themed to avoid generic diagram look
large graphs require performance and layout review

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Use for analytical graph exploration rather than authoring/editing pipelines.
tradeoffs: less natural for app-builder node editing
needs separate layout and interaction design

bannedFallbacks: static image diagram for interactive workflow
node cards without edges for graph workflow

domains.label: Rich Text And Research Documents

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Research desks need editable documents, structured notes, and script artifacts. Textareas are not sufficient for Tier 3.
tradeoffs: requires document schema decisions
collaboration/cloud features may require separate review

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Use when we want lower-level editor control and are willing to own more of the editor product surface.
tradeoffs: more custom build work
less turnkey for research workflows

bannedFallbacks: large textarea as primary research desk

domains.label: Image And Thumbnail Generation

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Automated thumbnails require deterministic server-side rendering, guardrails, sizing, and file output. Browser-only canvas is not enough for the pipeline.
tradeoffs: not interactive
must be paired with visual QA and asset manifest checks

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Use for analytical image processing where sharp is not enough.
tradeoffs: less standard for production thumbnail compositing
pipeline performance must be tested

bannedFallbacks: manual-only image export for production package

domains.label: Interactive Canvas Editing

libraryCandidates.whyUse: A human-adjustable thumbnail or post editor needs layer manipulation, not static form controls.
tradeoffs: browser-only
server export still needs a rendering backend such as sharp or Remotion

libraryCandidates.whyUse: A mature alternative if Konva cannot support a required editing workflow.
tradeoffs: React integration and state control require review
can drift from dashboard-kit patterns if not wrapped

bannedFallbacks: manual pixel positioning without safe bounds

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Video packages need reusable templates and previews. Plain FFmpeg scripts are too low-level for product-grade creative automation.
tradeoffs: heavier runtime
render infrastructure and licensing must be reviewed

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Keep FFmpeg as the low-level media operation layer even when Remotion owns templates.
tradeoffs: not a UI or template system
hard to maintain complex visuals as scripts only

domains.label: Forms And Validation

libraryCandidates.whyUse: Forms should have typed contracts, validation, dirty state, and submission proof. Visual-only forms are not sufficient.
tradeoffs: requires shared form component wrappers
schema design must be owned by each data domain

libraryCandidates.whyUse: A fallback for legacy projects already using Formik.
tradeoffs: less aligned with current schema-first TypeScript standard
heavier than needed for many dashboard forms

bannedFallbacks: approval/decline without reason capture when required

maturityWork.label: Build shared wrappers before downstream redesigns
maturityWork.whyItMatters: Libraries improve behavior only when the design kit wraps them. Direct project usage creates another drift vector.
maturityWork.requiredOutcome: Every default library has at least one @hermes/dashboard-kit wrapper component before a project can claim T3C for that domain.

maturityWork.label: Make validation screenshot-aware
maturityWork.whyItMatters: Static checks cannot prove overflow, clipped labels, unreadable themes, or generic-looking charts.
maturityWork.requiredOutcome: Tier 3 validation uses Playwright evidence to verify axes, legends, toolbars, empty states, and responsive layout.

maturityWork.label: Score each component family independently
maturityWork.whyItMatters: A dashboard can have a strong shell but weak charts or forms. The score must expose the weak family.
maturityWork.requiredOutcome: Dashboard maturity reports include family scores for shell, tables, charts, forms, calendars, workflows, proof states, and domain widgets.

maturityWork.label: Require a domain-library admission RFC
maturityWork.whyItMatters: New dependencies have long-term license, bundle, accessibility, and design-system costs.
maturityWork.requiredOutcome: Any new domain library includes an RFC with alternatives, proof, wrapper plan, and maintenance owner.

maturityWork.label: Scan downstream project usage
maturityWork.whyItMatters: A registry is not enforcement unless projects are checked for direct/local usage and missing wrappers.
maturityWork.requiredOutcome: CI warns or fails when registered projects use domain libraries directly outside approved wrappers.

maturityWork.label: Convert references into component requirements
maturityWork.whyItMatters: Mobbin screenshots do not improve UI unless they become extracted patterns, acceptance criteria, and reusable components.
maturityWork.requiredOutcome: Each major component family has reference evidence, mapped component variants, and visual acceptance criteria.
